body.heading: Expertise is everywhere
paragraphs: We tend to reserve the word 'expert' for famous people, but mastery is quietly all around: the market trader who wraps produce at astonishing speed, the grandparent who can judge dough by touch, the mechanic who diagnoses by sound.
Noticing this changes how you move through the world. Every workplace becomes a small museum of skills, and most of them took years to build.

body.heading: Watch first, ask well
paragraphs: If you get the chance, watch someone work before asking questions; you will ask better ones. 'How do you know when it is ready?' and 'What do beginners always get wrong?' tend to unlock the good stories.
Be brief, be grateful, and respect a no. People are usually pleased to be asked about their craft, especially by someone who has clearly been paying attention.

takeaway: Notice the mastery in ordinary jobs, and ask the questions that unlock it.
